Join−> https://t.me/thehindu000 World Geography General Studies CB–175 The World Climate *Climate is the average weather in a place over a certain period of time. It is determined by the daily weather conditions of a place (like temperature, rainfall, winds, humidity, air pressure etc) persisting over a long duration of time. * Earth has been basically divided into three climatic zones – Tropical Zone, Temperate Zone and Frigid Zone. These zones extend from the equator towards poles. * The continent of Asia extends from equator to North Poles. As a result, all types of climates are found here. Diﬀ erent climates are found in diﬀ erent parts of the world. Place having same climates are called climatic Regions and they are as follows: *Equatorial Climate – Found in between 5o to 10o North and south of the equator. The temperature remains high in this region all throughout the year. As a result, the region remains humid and the region receives rainfall afternoon. The ﬂ ora of the region consists of broadleaf evergreen trees like Gutta Percha, Rubber, Ebony, Palm, Boss, Bet, Mahogany, Sandal, Sinkona, etc. The regions under this climate include – Amazon Basin, Congo Basin of Africa, Guinea Coast, Eastern island groups, and eastern middle Americans (Panama, Costa- Rica, Nicaragua, Honduras, Guatemala). z Tropical Monsoonal Climatic Region – The region extends from 5o to 30o on both the hemisphere. The region lies in the route of trade winds. Places included in this region are – Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, Eastern Coastal Regions of Africa, South-Eastern coastal parts of USA, Northern parts of Australia etc. z Sahara Type of Climate – Also known as a tropical dry desert type of climate. The climate extends between 15o to 30o latitudes on both the sides of the equator in the western parts of the continent. There are two distinct seasons in this type of climate, the summer season and the winter season. Seasons are distinguished based on temperature. The average temperature of the summers is between 30o-35oC. According to the reading of NASA’s satellite (2003-2009) Dasht-e- Lut desert of Iran was the hottest place on the planet based on surface temperature. Highest recorded temperature was 70.7oC. Places under Sahara type of Climate includes – Thar desert and Arabian Peninsula of Asia, Sahara and Kalahari deserts of Africa, Western deserts of Australia. z Savanna Type of Climate – the temperature of the equatorial type of climate and savanna type of climate are some more the same. Since the savanna type of climate lies between the equatorial type of climate and tropical desert climate, the region is dominated by grasslands. Savanna type of climate is also called Sudan type of climate. There is a distinct dry and moist season however the temperature is high throughout the year. The places included in this region are – Venezuela, Colombia, Guyana, South-Central Brazil, and Paraguay. The maximum extension of Savanna type of climate in Africa is found in Sudan and in Australia, its maximum extension is in the Northern part. z Mediterannean Type of Climate: Also known as sub- tropical dry summer type of climate. Since this type of climate is found near the Mediterranean Sea hence it is known as Mediterranean of Climate. Mediterranean type of Climate is found between 30o to 40o latitudes on both the hemisphere on the western parts of the continents. Maximum rainfall occurs in winters. Summers are dry and winters are wet. The summer winds are dry in nature. The places included under the Mediterranean type of climate are – river valleys of France, southern Italy, Greece, Western Turkey, Western Israel, and North Western Africa which includes Algeria, Southern California of North America, Central Chile, and south-western part of South Africa. z Steppe Type of Climate – This type of climate is found in the temperate grassland regions. This type of climate is found in the middle Latitudes in the central parts of the continent. The annual range of temperature is high and annual rainfall is between 250 to 750 milimeter. Places included in steppe type of climate are – Grasslands of USA and Canada, Grasslands of South Australia and Eurasia. z Western European Climate – Found between 40o to 65o latitudes on both the hemisphere in the western part of the continents. The average temperature is between 15o-21oC. There is a good amount of rainfall in this climate however rainfall increases in winters as compared to summers. Places included in western European type of Climate are – North Western Europe, Western Norway, Denmark, North Western Germany, France Oregon and Washington in the USA, British Columbia in Canada, Chile and New Zealand. z St. Lawrence Type of Climate – It is a moist continental type of climate, found on the eastern ends of the continent, predominantly in the Northern Hemisphere between 45o to 65o latitudes. There is a good amount of rainfall throughout the year but more in summers as compared to winters. The places included under St. Lawrence type of climate are – parts of Argentina, Manchuria region of China, St. Lawrence Valley of America, Coastal provinces of Canada. z Taiga Type of climate – Also known as a Siberian type of Climate which comes under Microthermal climate. The winters are long and the summers are of short duration. The Join−> https://t.me/thehindu000 CB–176 General Studies World Geography 10oC temperature of a region determines the Northern limit of Taiga. Winter season is approximately 8 months long during which the temperature remains well below freezing point. *In Polar regions lowest temperature was recorded in Greenland – 69.6oC (-93.3oF) in February 1993. * The lowest temperature of the world was recorded in Vostok in Eastern Antarctica on 21st July, 1983, which was – 89.2oC (-128.6oF). According to latest updates, June, 2018 Geophysical Research published that on earth minimum temperature recorded at Mid-Antartica i.e. –98oC (–144oF) before this, the lowest temperature recorded is from eastern Africa on 31st July 2013 which stood at – 93.0oC. The average annual rainfall in Taiga type of climate is between 370 to 600 milimeters, however, maximum rainfall is in the form of snow. Places included in this type of climate are Alaska of USA, Northernmost parts of Canada, from Scandinavia in the west to Siberia in the east, in Eurasia. z Tundra Type of Climate – They have the least vegetation and are found in Polar and Arctic regions. The ecological productivity is minimum. In Tundra type of climate, there is a deﬁ ciency in solar heat as a result the temperature remains very low all throughout the year. The annual average rainfall is less than 400 mm. Tundras extends from the southern limits of northern glaciers to southern limits of Taiga in the South, and includes the regions of America and Eurasia. Tundra only supports limited ﬂ oras like Lichens and Moss Flora that can tolerate cold polar climate for example, that of high mountains and Alpines are called Hekistotherms. 1. Variations in the length of day and night time from season to season are due to – 1. The earth’s rotation on its axis 2. The earth’s revolution around the sun in an elliptical manner. 3. Latitudinal position of the place. 4. Revolution of the earth on axis Which of the above-mentioned statement/statements is/are correct? (a) 1 only (b) 2 and 4 only (c) 1, 2 and 3 (d) 1 and 3 only I.A.S. (Pre) 2013 Ans. (b) Earth is tilted on its axis. If Earth would not have been tilted on its axis, then days and nights would have been equal everywhere. In the same way, if Earth would not have been revolving around the sun, then there would have been always longer days and shorter nights in one hemisphere and longer nights and shorter days in the other hemisphere.
